stories.title: Anthropic’s Opus 4.6 is a smut-machine
stories.simple_summary: Anthropic built Claude to refuse making sexually explicit content, but researchers found it's not very hard to trick it into doing so anyway.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use Claude for work, be aware it has safety guardrails, but they're not perfect — this mostly matters to Anthropic's engineers to fix, not to you.

stories.title: Nvidia partners with data center developer Cloverleaf
stories.simple_summary: Nvidia (a computer chip company) is investing money in companies that build data centers for AI.
stories.why_it_matters: This matters to investors in Nvidia stock — not something an ordinary person or small-business owner needs to know about.

stories.title: Over 1 million people have clicked LinkedIn’s AI slop button
stories.simple_summary: LinkedIn added a button where people can mark posts that look like they were written by AI instead of a real person, and over a million people have used it so far.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use LinkedIn and see boring, fake-looking AI-written posts, you can now flag them to help clean up the platform.

stories.title: Nvidia just showed that the harness, not the AI model, is now the real hero
stories.simple_summary: Nvidia research shows that the way you set up and control an AI tool matters just as much as how smart the AI itself is.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly technical information for engineers and AI developers — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: The DOJ is investigating a16z. What does this mean for venture capital?
stories.simple_summary: The Department of Justice is investigating a big venture capital company called Andreessen Horowitz because some of its leaders sit on the boards of competing companies at the same time.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a legal investigation about conflicts of interest in the investing world — it doesn't directly affect small-business owners or everyday people.

stories.title: Starcloud raises $250 million for orbital data centers as launch options dry up
stories.simple_summary: A company called Starcloud raised a huge amount of money to build data centers in space for AI companies.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a very experimental, futuristic idea — not something relevant to ordinary people or small-business owners right now.

stories.title: Major YouTube creators are facing backlash for accepting AI money
stories.simple_summary: Some popular video creators on YouTube posted videos showing AI video-making tools, and people criticized them for promoting AI without being honest about it.
stories.why_it_matters: Be cautious when watching online content creators — if they're showing off a new tool, check whether they were paid to promote it.

stories.title: AI data startup Micro1 reaches $500M gross run rate amid AI training boom
stories.simple_summary: A startup company that sells training data for AI is growing very fast because AI companies need lots and lots of data.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors — the underlying point is that AI companies have huge appetite for data, which could affect what gets collected about you.

stories.title: OpenAI is gaining on Anthropic with business users, new data indicates
stories.simple_summary: Businesses keep switching between using ChatGPT and Claude (made by Anthropic) depending on which one seems better at the moment.
stories.why_it_matters: This matters to investors wondering if companies will stick with one AI tool long-term — not something you need to worry about.

stories.title: ChatGPT can now send texts for you with new Apple Messages plug-in
stories.simple_summary: ChatGPT can now write text messages for you if you use an iPhone and want it to.
stories.why_it_matters: If you have an iPhone and find texting tedious, you could try this feature to have AI draft your messages for you before you send them.

stories.title: Google Discover is getting an AI chatbot-tuned feed
stories.simple_summary: Google is adding an AI feature that learns what kinds of news and information you like to see, and automatically adjusts your feed based on what you ask for.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use Google's Discover feed, you'll get a new way to control what shows up — but Google will still be tracking your preferences to do this.

stories.title: OK, can we actually cool data centers with our pee?
stories.simple_summary: Someone joked about using wastewater to cool AI data centers instead of clean drinking water, and it turns out the idea isn't completely crazy.
stories.why_it_matters: This is an interesting environmental idea researchers are exploring, but it's early-stage and doesn't affect you yet.
